title: Impact of Surprise Electoral Outcomes on Industry Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
To analyze the impact of surprise electoral outcomes on industry returns, we will use an Event Study approach. This method is suitable for assessing the effect of a specific event (in this case, the surprise electoral outcome) on the financial performance of industries. The key assumption of the Event Study method is that the event date (election day) is exogenously determined and uncorrelated with other factors that could affect industry returns. In this scenario, we will calculate the Cumulative Abnormal Returns (CAR) around the event date to capture the immediate impact of the surprise electoral outcome on industry-level financial performance.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Load the dataset
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s64_data.csv")

# Calculate abnormal returns
data$abn_ret <- data$ret - data$mkt_ret

# Calculate cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) for each industry around the event date
car_data <- data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  mutate(car = cumsum(abn_ret))

# Calculate the average CAR across all industries for the event window (-10 to 10 days)
avg_car_data <- car_data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -10 & event_day <= 10) %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(avg_car = mean(car))

# Print the average CAR for the event window
print(avg_car_data)

# Basic robustness check: Calculate the average CAR for a shorter event window (-5 to 5 days)
avg_car_short_data <- car_data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -5 & event_day <= 5) %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(avg_car = mean(car))

# Print the average CAR for the shorter event window
print(avg_car_short_data)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) to be significantly different from zero around the event date, indicating an immediate impact of the surprise electoral outcome on industry-level financial performance. The sign and magnitude of the CAR will depend on the direction and size of the unexpected election results. For example, if the surprise electoral outcome is perceived as positive for certain industries, we expect to see a positive CAR for those industries, indicating an increase in their stock prices relative to the market returns. Conversely, if the outcome is perceived as negative, we expect to see a negative CAR. The approximate magnitude of the CAR will depend on the extent to which the surprise electoral outcome affects the industries' financial performance.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Analyze stock returns before and after the election event to isolate the impact of the surprise outcome.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The unexpected election result led to a negative impact on industry-level CAR.
